page.text:
Just as De Morgan's laws govern the interaction between negation,
conjunction, and disjunction in propositional logic, an identical duality
governs the negation of quantifiers. Negating a universal claim produces
an existential claim, and negating an existential claim produces a
universal claim:
$$\neg \forall x \in D \, P(x) \iff \exists x \in D \, \neg P(x)$$
$$\neg \exists x \in D \, P(x) \iff \forall x \in D \, \neg P(x)$$

To deny that every swan is white is not to claim that every swan is
black; it is to assert the existence of at least one non-white swan.
Dually, to deny that a system of equations has a solution is to assert
that every proposed candidate fails to solve it.
